subject: Re: HelixBank - enterprise requirements: rollback controls + audit log semantics (Optimize config changes)
related_links: Redwood Docs (draft): Config history + rollback + audit logs (link shared in-thread)
body:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@helixbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: GRC Inbox <grc@helixbank.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 4, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: HelixBank - enterprise requirements: rollback controls + audit log semantics (Optimize config changes)

Hi Marissa,

Following up on the incident discussion last week, we need to validate two items for our change management controls before we can move Optimize recommendations into production:

1) Audit logs
- What specific events are logged for config changes and rollbacks?
- Are the logs immutable? What is your retention period?
- What fields are captured (actor, role, before/after, scope, correlation/request ids)?
- Can the logs be exported to our SIEM (Splunk) and do you support tenant-scoped access?

2) RBAC and approvals
- Which roles can apply config changes vs rollback?
- Do you support separation of duties (e.g., operator can propose change but cannot approve/apply)?
- Do you support a required justification / ticket id on apply/rollback?

If you have a sample event payload and/or a permissions matrix we can attach to our internal assessment, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Security Architecture (Cloud & AI)
HelixBank


---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@helixbank.com>
Cc: GRC Inbox <grc@helixbank.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 4, 2025 at 11:03 AM
Subject: Re: HelixBank - enterprise requirements: rollback controls + audit log semantics (Optimize config changes)

Hi Priya,

Yes — we can share both a sample audit event taxonomy and the RBAC permissions we’re implementing for Optimize config versioning + one-click rollback.

A few quick answers inline (more detail + attachments to follow by EOD tomorrow):

Audit logs
- We log every attempt + outcome for apply and rollback (attempted / succeeded / failed), with actor identity, tenant, scope (customer/deployment/region/route/model), version ids, request id, and an immutable event id.
- Retention: baseline 90 days in-product; enterprise add-on extends retention (typical 1 year+). Export options available.
- SIEM: we support streaming to customer endpoints in enterprise plans (webhook + optional S3 export; Splunk is supported via HEC on your side).

RBAC
- We’re introducing separate permissions for apply vs rollback (and for viewing history).
- We can require an external ticket reference (e.g., ServiceNow/Jira) on apply/rollback; it is stored as metadata and emitted in the audit events.

Let me loop in our Console/Tooling lead and Security Ops to make sure we send you the right level of detail and avoid overpromising on items that are in-flight.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Product, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference

They specifically asked about immutability, retention, SIEM export, SoD, and required justification / ticket id.

Dylan/Chloe: what’s true today vs Phase 1 vs Phase 2?

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Fiona McCarthy <fiona@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Nov 5, 2025 at 9:18 AM
Subject: Re: Fwd: HelixBank - enterprise requirements: rollback controls + audit log semantics (Optimize config changes)

Marissa — quick status + proposed wording.

What’s true in Phase 1 (version history + rollback + audit events):
- Audit events emitted for:
  - optimize.config.apply_attempted
  - optimize.config.apply_succeeded
  - optimize.config.apply_failed
  - optimize.config.rollback_attempted
  - optimize.config.rollback_succeeded
  - optimize.config.rollback_failed
- Each event includes tenant_id, actor (user_id + email), auth context (role ids), target scope (deployment/region/cluster/route/model), from_version_id/to_version_id, request_id, and outcome.
- “Immutable”: events are append-only once emitted. We should phrase as “append-only, tamper-evident storage in our audit log pipeline” rather than “cryptographically immutable” unless Security signs off.

RBAC:
- New permissions:
  - optimize.config.read_history
  - optimize.config.apply
  - optimize.config.rollback
- Recommended default roles:
  - Tenant Admin: read/apply/rollback
  - Operator (SRE): read/rollback
  - Viewer/Auditor: read
- Separation of duties (two-person approval) is not in initial release. We *do* support requiring metadata (ticket link + freeform reason) with apply/rollback.

SIEM export:
- We can provide “Audit Log Export” via webhook (JSON) and/or S3 delivery for enterprise; not all tenants have it enabled by default. We should keep it conditional.

Chloe can help with sample payloads. I’ll draft a permissions matrix today.

— Dylan

From: Fiona McCarthy <fiona@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Nov 5, 2025 at 10:02 AM
Subject: Re: Fwd: HelixBank - enterprise requirements: rollback controls + audit log semantics (Optimize config changes)

+1 to Dylan’s wording.

Please avoid “immutable” in the absolute sense. Suggested language:
- “Append-only audit events. Events cannot be edited via product APIs or console once written.”
- “Access controlled; export is tenant-scoped.”

Retention guidance:
- Standard: 90 days available in-console.
- Export/extended retention: enterprise option (contracted). If HelixBank needs 1+ year, we should propose export to their system of record.

Redaction:
- Don’t promise full request/response bodies. We log config diffs (sanitized) + identifiers; we do not log prompt contents.

If they ask about evidence: we can share sample JSON payloads and our SOC2 report under NDA (separate process).

Fiona McCarthy
Security Operations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@helixbank.com>
Cc: GRC Inbox <grc@helixbank.com>
Date: Wed, Nov 5, 2025 at 2:27 PM
Subject: Re: HelixBank - enterprise requirements: rollback controls + audit log semantics (Optimize config changes)

Hi Priya,

Thanks for laying out the requirements clearly. We pulled together (1) a sample audit event packet and (2) an RBAC permissions matrix for Optimize config history/apply/rollback.

Attachments:
- Redwood_Optimize_Config_Audit_Events_Sample_v0.6.pdf
- RBAC_Permissions_Matrix_Optimize_Config_Apply_Rollback_v0.4.xlsx

Answers to your questions:

1) Audit logs
Events logged
- We emit append-only audit events for apply and rollback, including attempted/succeeded/failed outcomes.
- Event types (representative):
  - optimize.config.apply_attempted / apply_succeeded / apply_failed
  - optimize.config.rollback_attempted / rollback_succeeded / rollback_failed

Fields captured
- Actor: user_id + email, plus auth context (role ids) at the time of action
- What: from_version_id/to_version_id + a sanitized config diff summary (and a full config version hash)
- Where: tenant + scope (deployment mode, region/cluster, route/model)
- When: server timestamps
- Correlation: request_id and event_id
- Metadata: required “reason” text; optional linked ticket id/URL (recommended)

Immutability / tamper resistance
- Audit events are append-only. Once written, they cannot be edited via Console or product APIs.

Retention
- Baseline: 90 days viewable in Console.
- Enterprise options include extended retention and/or export (typically we recommend exporting to your SIEM/system of record for 1+ year policies).

Export / SIEM
- For enterprise deployments, we support tenant-scoped audit log export (webhook JSON and/or object storage delivery depending on environment). We can coordinate Splunk details with your team once we’re past solutioning.

2) RBAC and approvals
Roles / permissions
- We use explicit permissions for:
  - optimize.config.read_history
  - optimize.config.apply
  - optimize.config.rollback
- Common enterprise mapping:
  - Viewer/Auditor: read only
  - Operator (on-call/SRE): read + rollback
  - Admin: read + apply + rollback

Separation of duties
- Two-person approvals (propose vs approve/apply) are not in the initial GA scope for this feature.

Justification / ticket id
- We support requiring an operator-provided “reason” for apply/rollback; additionally, we support attaching a ticket id/URL (ServiceNow/Jira/etc.) and emitting it in the audit event.

If helpful, we can do a 30-minute working session with your GRC + platform folks to align on what evidence you need for your internal control.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Product, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@helixbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: GRC Inbox <grc@helixbank.com>
Date: Thu, Nov 6, 2025 at 1:16 PM
Subject: Re: HelixBank - enterprise requirements: rollback controls + audit log semantics (Optimize config changes)

Marissa,

This is helpful — thank you.

Two follow-ups from our controls team:
1) Can you confirm whether rollback is restricted to known-good versions only (i.e., an operator can’t “edit” during rollback)?
2) For export: if we take the enterprise export option, can events be scoped to our tenant only and delivered near-real-time (minutes)?

Also, please confirm whether any “config diff” includes customer prompts or user content. (We assume no, but need it in writing.)

Priya


---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@helixbank.com>
Cc: GRC Inbox <grc@helixbank.com>
Date: Thu, Nov 6, 2025 at 4:41 PM
Subject: Re: HelixBank - enterprise requirements: rollback controls + audit log semantics (Optimize config changes)

Priya,

Confirmed on all three:

1) Rollback semantics
- Rollback is to a previously created, stored config version only (whole-config rollback). Operators select a prior version id; they do not edit fields as part of rollback.

2) Export scope + latency
- Export is tenant-scoped (only your tenant’s audit events).
- Delivery is near-real-time; in practice it’s typically minutes (dependent on destination and connectivity).

3) Prompts / user content
- Optimize config diffs and audit events do not include customer prompts or end-user content. They capture optimization configuration values/changes (e.g., batching/caching/quantization/routing knobs) plus metadata like ticket link and scope.

If you’d like, we can add a short statement reflecting #3 into the security addendum for your review.

Best,
Marissa
